machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.3 (bundled, static); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: 7.25.21 and 7.25.22 each built from their own tree: a git worktree of the 7.25.21 tag with the same .config and compiler, where only the kernel libraries, modules/c/test, the benchmarks of performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built. outputs_ext was shared between the two trees: linux-ext-libs did not change in this release. Measured: the benchmarks of performance/c/ and the ctest binaries test_topic_pkey_integer, test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator2 and test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5. The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run: 8 rounds, 24 for the three ctest binaries. Mean +- standard deviation (median). No module was padded or relinked: a whole-release build also moves where the code lands, so a change of a few percent is not told apart from placement.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.25.22 are its side of the A/B run (the code of the tag, built from the main tree before the version bump): 8 rounds of the benchmarks of performance/c/, 24 of the three ctest binaries, a sync and a 3 s pause before each run, no CPU pinning. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass.

story.title: Yuneta 7.25.22: two reviews closed, and a forced delete 39% faster
story.lead: 7.25.22 closes two reviews -- of 7.25.21, and of the fixes made for it -- and the open defects of the list it inherited: the agents run as native systemd units, a connection can be dropped from any callback of TLS or TCP without a use of freed memory, a yuno alive but not connected can be killed, the rt_disk followers of timeranger2 hear what they used to lose (a key directory they could not watch, an end of their events they could not count), C_AUTHZ and the IdP stop handing roles and keys to whoever asks, and a stats reset resets. Measured against 7.25.21 on the same machine, each release built from its own tree, the two run alternately: a forced delete in a treedb takes 39% less time, because a delete no longer walks every open key. Four other figures moved beyond their spread on code that did not change -- two a little slower, two faster -- and are said, not claimed: that is where the code landed.

hero.text: of the time of a forced delete in a treedb of 100 000 nodes: the descriptors of the deleted key are closed without walking every key that holds one.

tiles: TLS echo through the gobj stack
story.append_note: -1.9% against 7.25.21 (228,532), on the same append code: placement, see the A/B; 24 alternated rounds
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built twice, from the tree of each release, and the two binaries run alternately: 8 rounds, 24 for the three timeranger2 tests. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, and what it buys.
story.no_prices: None. No change of 7.25.22 makes a measured path slower. Two figures moved beyond their spread in that direction: 600 000 appends (-1.9% appends per second, -1.6% with a live reader) and a treedb update in memory (+5.0% of time). Neither path changed in this release -- the append code, `tr_treedb.c`, `kwid.c` and jansson are the same -- and on the same code the appends to a store of many keys moved the other way (-8.5% of time), as the update in memory did in the report of 7.25.21 (-5.2%). Both releases are built whole, so the code lands at other addresses: that is placement, not speed, and it is said with its figure.
